contribution_assessment: Adds an entirely new institutional/social-reality layer to the Knowledge Space model not present anywhere earlier in the batch: the X-counts-as-Y-in-C / Status(X,Y,C) formalization, deontic power, collective intentionality, institutional facts as relational networks, the primacy-of-process-over-object argument (directly extending the Merricks object-vs-process question), and a major refinement of the earlier language-is-merely-expression conclusion into an expressive-vs-constitutive language distinction with direct consequences for how KnowledgeOS must record authoritative institutional utterances.

summary: Refines a user proposal that 'knowledge = capacity to write information' into a three-stage chain (Infinite Knowledge Space -> Information -> Knowledge Capacity -> Knowledge Projection), rejecting the narrower formulation because a person can know something without being able to write it down and an institutional system can preserve information without 'knowing' it epistemically. Formalizes Knowledge Capacity as K=(B,L,R,C,P) (boundary/level-of-abstraction/epistemic-regime/contextual-capacity/participant-capacity) producing a Knowledge Projection K(Omega); ties this to the prior Floridi (LoA/observables), Gärdenfors (epistemic state/expansion/revision/contraction), Dretske (information vs. its physical/linguistic encoding), and Searle (institutional context determining what counts as what) lenses; distinguishes three separate capacities -- information capacity (storage/bandwidth/memory/sensor resolution), epistemic capacity (reasoning/awareness/inference/uncertainty handling/causal understanding), and expressive capacity (language/symbols/documents/models/code/diagrams) -- illustrated with worked capacity profiles for a person, an LLM, and a database; proposes a revised definition of KnowledgeOS as preserving and exposing the structures through which a participant constructs/scopes/represents/evaluates/relates/revises/communicates a projection, rather than 'storing knowledge'; and closes with a refined single-sentence definition of knowledge plus an open question on whether 'capacity' itself is a Kernel primitive or derived from participant/boundary/representation/regime/resources.
contribution_assessment: Introduces a genuinely new construct not present earlier in the batch -- Knowledge Capacity as an intermediate layer between raw Information and a Knowledge Projection, formalized as K=(B,L,R,C,P) -- and a three-way information/epistemic/expressive capacity distinction with worked person/LLM/database profiles that is directly actionable for comparing heterogeneous KnowledgeOS participants; closes by explicitly nominating 'capacity' as the next Zero-Lens elimination-test candidate.
